item.title: Lessons from Two Novartis Oligonucleotide Failures
item.description: Novartis’ two recent Phase III failures of oligonucleotide drugs have broken my preconception about this class of therapeutics — that suppressing target expression will, with high probability, translate into clinical efficacy. This view is essentially a static worldview: it assumes that flipping a single switch is enough to reverse a disease outcome. In reality, however, outcomes are shaped dynamically. There may be an initial trigger or a dominant factor, but as the disease progresses, multiple forces and effects compete and interact with one another.

item.title: About
item.description: I am currently a migrant worker in the biopharmaceutical industry, still drifting in Beijing. I did my undergraduate studies at an agricultural university in Wuhan, and earned my PhD at a university on Chengfu Road in Haidian District, Beijing. In my spare time I enjoy films, podcasts, and reading. Here I will share my everyday reflections, reading notes, investment case studies, and thoughts on the pharmaceutical industry. Feel free to reach out by email.
